/-!
# Conjecture 8.59

by V. M. Poletskikh, I. V. Protasov

Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper closed
normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

Here a group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent,
and, as usual in topological group theory, locally compact groups are assumed to be
Hausdorff.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question quantified over all locally compact (Hausdorff) topological groups G that are locally nilpotent (every finitely generated subgroup nilpotent) and in which every proper closed normal subgroup is compact; 'proper' means ≠ G, and the asked-for subgroup must be simultaneously open, compact and normal (it may be trivial or all of G, e.g. when G itself is compact).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the mathematically identical proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ Hausdorff locally compact topological group G (Type), [every f.g. subgroup nilpotent] → [every normal, closed, ≠ ⊤ subgroup compact] → ∃ subgroup that is simultaneously normal, open and compact. This matches the statement and the decomposition notes (proper = ≠ G; witness may be ⊥ or ⊤; positive answer = 'yes for all such G'). Checked boundary cases: trivial group satisfies hypothesis and conclusion via ⊤; ℝ, ℤ fail the hypothesis (non-compact proper closed subgroups) so the hypothesis is not vacuous; ℚ_p and discrete quasicyclic groups satisfy it and have an open compact normal subgroup, consistent with the problem being open. c07 chosen because it names the concept via a bespoke, docstringed `IsLocallyNilpotent` (Mathlib has no group-theoretic locally-nilpotent predicate; pattern matches Kourovka/1_40.lean's IsEngelGroup) and includes two compiling API lemmas, as CONTRIBUTING requests for bespoke definitions. My only edit: made `G` implicit in `IsLocallyNilpotent.isNilpotent` (Mathlib style, since `hG` is explicit). c01/c03/c06/c08 (inlined) and c02/c04/c05 (bespoke def) are equally faithful; the choice among them is purely stylistic.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.59

by V. M. Poletskikh, I. V. Protasov

Suppose that, in a locally compact locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper closed
normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

Here a group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent,
and, as usual in topological group theory, locally compact groups are assumed to be
Hausdorff.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.59»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- Every nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNilpotent_of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finitely generated locally nilpotent group is nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.isNilpotent {G : Type*} [Group G] [Group.FG G]
    (hG : IsLocallyNilpotent G) : Group.IsNilpotent G :=
  Group.isNilpotent_top.mp (hG ⊤ (Group.fg_def.mp ‹_›))

/--
Suppose that, in a locally compact (Hausdorff) locally nilpotent group $G$, all proper
closed normal subgroups are compact. Does $G$ contain an open compact normal subgroup?

Here "proper" means different from $G$ itself; the open compact normal subgroup asked
for is allowed to be trivial or to be all of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«8.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
      [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      IsLocallyNilpotent G →
      (∀ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal → N ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (N : Set G) → IsCompact (N : Set G)) →
      ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ IsOpen (N : Set G) ∧ IsCompact (N : Set G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.59»

items: 'Locally compact group' is read, per the standard convention in topological group theory (and the decomposition notes), as a Hausdorff locally compact topological group: `[IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]`. Dropping `T2Space` would quantify over a strictly larger class of groups.

'Locally nilpotent' is formalized as: every finitely generated subgroup `H` (as `Subgroup.FG`) is nilpotent as a group (`Group.IsNilpotent ↥H`, i.e. its upper central series reaches ⊤ in finitely many steps). This is the standard definition.

'Proper' is `N ≠ ⊤`; the trivial subgroup counts as a proper closed normal subgroup (compact anyway). Closed/open/compact are stated on the carrier set `(N : Set G)`; an open subgroup is automatically closed so no closedness is added to the conclusion.

The asked-for subgroup is only required to be normal, open and compact; it may be `⊥` (discrete G) or `⊤` (compact G), matching the decomposition notes. The trivial group satisfies the hypotheses vacuously and the conclusion via `⊤`.

The bespoke definition `IsLocallyNilpotent` is generic and would normally belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/; it is kept in the problem file only because the task restricts all output to the single candidate file (same pattern as Kourovka/1_40.lean, which keeps `IsEngelGroup` in the problem file).
The group type is quantified in universe `Type`, matching the other Kourovka files.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) 'locally compact group' is taken to include Hausdorff (T2Space), the standard convention in topological group theory and the Kourovka Notebook (and stipulated by the decomposition notes); dropping T2 would quantify over a larger class. (2) 'locally nilpotent' is read algebraically (every finitely generated subgroup nilpotent), the standard definition and the one stipulated in the notes; a topological variant (e.g. compactly generated closed subgroups pro-nilpotent) would be a different statement, but nothing in the source suggests it. (3) 'proper' = ≠ G; the trivial subgroup is a permitted proper closed normal subgroup (harmless: it is compact). The witness subgroup is not required to be proper or nontrivial, per the source and notes. No candidate omitted the slot; there were no decomposition objections. Final file compiles under `lake env lean` with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning. The bespoke `IsLocallyNilpotent` is generic and would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/ with an index entry; it is kept in the problem file because the pipeline output is a single file (same as Kourovka/1_40.lean's IsEngelGroup).
